title: Security
loadFailed: Could not read the state of your second factor.

totp.title: Two-factor authentication
totp.description: An authenticator app shows a six-digit code that changes every 30 seconds. With it switched on, a stolen password on its own is not enough to sign in as you.

status.on: On. Signing in asks for a code from your authenticator app.

scan.description: Scan this with your authenticator app, or type the secret in by hand. Then enter the code it shows, together with your current password.

qr.alt: QR code for pairing an authenticator app. The same secret is written out below as text.

secret.hint: No camera? Type this into the app instead:

code.label: Code from the app
code.description: Six digits. It changes every 30 seconds — if it expires while you type, use the next one.

password.label: Your current password
password.description: Asked for so that a stolen browser session cannot attach somebody else's authenticator to your account.

failed.title: Two-factor authentication was not turned on
failed.lostAnswer: If you are seeing this after a connection dropped mid-confirmation, two-factor authentication may already be on and your recovery codes were never shown. Go to «Replace recovery codes» below: it asks for this same password and a code from the app, and it issues a fresh set.

warning.title: Worth knowing before you turn it on
warning.disable: Turning it off later needs the same two things signing in will: your current password and a code — from the app, or an unused recovery code. A stolen browser session cannot do it; neither can you, without one of the two.
warning.recoveryOnly: The recovery codes you get next are the only way back in if the phone is lost. They are stored as hashes, so nobody can look them up for you — not support, not whoever runs this server.
warning.lostAnswer: The codes are shown once, in the answer to the confirmation. If that answer never arrives — the connection drops, the tab closes — two-factor authentication is on and the codes are gone. A new set can still be issued from this page with your password and a code from the app.

disable.title: Turn off two-factor authentication
disable.description: Removes the second factor from this account. Signing in goes back to your password alone.

consequence.passwordOnly: Your password becomes the only thing between your account and anybody who learns it.
consequence.codes: Every recovery code you still have stops working and is deleted. The same ones cannot be brought back.
consequence.again: You can turn it on again whenever you like, but it starts from scratch: a new QR code to scan and a new set of ten codes to save.

code.label: Code from the app, or a recovery code
code.description: Six digits from your authenticator app — or, if the app is gone, one of the recovery codes you have not used yet.

failed.title: Two-factor authentication was not turned off

disable.done: Two-factor authentication is off. Your password is now the only thing that signs you in.

reset.title: Two-factor authentication
reset.description: If this person has lost both their authenticator app and every recovery code, resetting the second factor is the only way back into their account.

dialog.title: Reset this person's two-factor authentication?
dialog.description: This removes the second factor from the account of «{{email}}». You are not asked for their password or a code — your permission is the whole of the proof, so read the list below before confirming.

consequence.passwordOnly: Their password becomes the only thing between their account and anybody who learns it, until they set the second factor up again themselves.
consequence.codes: Every recovery code they still have stops working and is deleted. The same ones cannot be brought back.
consequence.sessions: Every session is closed — they are signed out on every device within a second, not at token expiry.
consequence.notified: They are emailed about it, and that notice cannot be switched off.
consequence.accessKept: Nothing else changes: the account stays active, keeps its roles, and can sign in again with the password alone. This is not a way to remove somebody's access.

reset.confirmLabel: Type the email address to confirm
reset.confirmHint: Type «{{email}}» — this lowers somebody's account to a password alone, and the row you came from is one mis-click away.

done.title: The second factor is off.
done.next: Turning it back on is theirs to do: tell them to open Security in their own settings and enrol again. Nobody else can do it for them.

already.title: This account had no second factor — nothing was changed
already.description: Two-factor authentication was already off before this run, so there was no session to close and no recovery code to delete. Nothing was written and nobody was emailed. This is what resetting the wrong person looks like, and what a second run looks like — not a failure.

codes.title: Recovery codes
codes.description: Ten one-time codes. Each one signs you in once, when the authenticator app is not available.

low.title: Running out of recovery codes
low.description_one: {{count}} code left. Replace the set while the app is still to hand — replacing needs a code from it.
low.description_other: {{count}} codes left. Replace the set while the app is still to hand — replacing needs a code from it.

none.title: No recovery codes left
none.description: Every code has been used. The authenticator app is now the only way in — issue a new set below while it still works. If the app goes too, only an administrator with the right to reset your second factor can let you back in.

regenerate.title: Replace recovery codes
regenerate.description: Issues ten new codes and destroys the old ones at the same moment. Use it when the codes are running low, when somebody else may have seen them, or when you never got to see them at all.

dialog.title: Your recovery codes
dialog.onceDescription: This is the only time these codes can be read. After this window closes they cannot be shown again — only hashes of them are kept. Download or print them now.
dialog.savedHint: Somewhere you can reach without this account: a password manager, a printout, a note kept safe.

file.header: Bad CRM recovery codes. Each code signs you in once, when your authenticator app is not available. Keep them somewhere you can reach without this account.

password.title: Password
password.description: Changing it signs out every other device at the same moment, and cancels any reset link that has been sent.

new.label: New password
new.description: At least 12 characters. Length is worth more than punctuation — a phrase you can remember beats a short word with symbols in it.

password.done: Password changed. Every other session has been signed out.

sessions.title: Where you are signed in
sessions.description: One entry per device holding a live session. Close any of them you do not recognise — it stops working within a second, not when its token expires.
sessions.loadFailed: Could not read the list of your sessions.

revoke.title: Close this session?
revoke.description: The session on «{{device}}» stops working immediately.

signOut.title: Sign out of this device?
signOut.description: This is the session you are using right now. Closing it signs you out here.

others.title: Close every other session?
others.description: Every device except this one is signed out. This one keeps working.

consequence.immediate: It stops working within a second — the next request it makes is refused, rather than waiting for its token to run out.
consequence.signInAgain: Whoever is using it has to sign in again with the password, and with the second factor if it is switched on.
consequence.noUndo: There is no undoing this. A session that is closed cannot be reopened.
consequence.here: This tab returns to the sign-in screen straight away. Nothing else about your account changes.

done.othersNone: There was nothing else open — this is the only session.
